fields.name: Glenfiddich
fields.description: The world's best-selling single malt, known for its fruity and balanced character. A pioneering distillery in promoting single malt whisky globally.

fields.name: The Glenlivet
fields.description: The first licensed distillery in the parish of Glenlivet, producing elegant and fruity Speyside malts. Often considered the definitive Speyside style.

fields.name: Macallan
fields.description: Renowned for sherry-cask matured whiskies with rich, complex flavors. One of the most prestigious and expensive single malts in the world.

fields.name: Aberlour
fields.description: Famous for double-cask maturation combining bourbon and sherry casks, creating rich and fruity whiskies. A favorite among sherry cask enthusiasts.

fields.name: Balvenie
fields.description: One of the few distilleries maintaining traditional floor maltings, producing honeyed and rich whiskies. Known for innovative cask finishing techniques.

fields.name: Glenfarclas
fields.description: One of Scotland's few remaining independent family-owned distilleries, producing powerful sherry-matured malts. Known for impressive vintage releases.

fields.name: Cragganmore
fields.description: Known for its complex and elegant character with unusual flat-topped stills. Selected as the Speyside representative in the Classic Malts range.

fields.name: Cardhu
fields.description: Founded by Helen Cumming, a pioneering woman in whisky, producing smooth and sweet single malts. The heart of Johnnie Walker blends.

fields.name: Knockando
fields.description: Produces elegant and delicate malts, traditionally bottled by season rather than age. An important component in J&B blends.

fields.name: Tamdhu
fields.description: Exclusively matured in sherry casks, producing rich and full-bodied Speyside malts. One of the few distilleries with working Saladin maltings.

fields.name: Tomintoul
fields.description: Scotland's highest distillery at 1,160 feet, producing gentle and approachable whiskies. Known for its peated expressions as well.

fields.name: Benrinnes
fields.description: Known for unique partial triple distillation and meaty, robust character. Primarily used for blending but cult-followed as a single malt.

fields.name: Dailuaine
fields.description: Produces robust, waxy malts mainly for Johnnie Walker blends. Rarely seen as a single malt but highly regarded by whisky enthusiasts.

fields.name: Mortlach
fields.description: The first legal distillery in Dufftown, producing meaty and complex malts through unique 2.81 times distillation. Known as the Beast of Dufftown.

fields.name: Dufftown
fields.description: A key malt in the Bells blend, producing sweet and malty whiskies. One of six distilleries in the town known as the whisky capital.

fields.name: Glendullan
fields.description: Produces grassy, floral malts for Old Parr and Singleton ranges. Known for technical innovation and clean spirit character.

fields.name: Strathisla
fields.description: The oldest continuously operating distillery in the Highlands, with picturesque pagoda roofs. The heart of the Chivas Regal blend.

fields.name: Glen Grant
fields.description: Known for light, delicate, and fruity whiskies with tall stills and purifier systems. One of Italy's favorite single malts.

fields.name: Longmorn
fields.description: Highly regarded by blenders and connoisseurs for rich, complex character. Often called one of the best unsung malts of Speyside.

fields.name: BenRiach
fields.description: Known for experimental cask finishes and both peated and unpeated expressions. Produces over 30 different styles of whisky.

fields.name: Glen Moray
fields.description: A former brewery converted to a distillery, producing approachable and fruity malts. Known for innovative cask finishing experiments.

fields.name: Miltonduff
fields.description: Produces clean, grassy spirit for Ballantine's blends. Once had unique Lomond stills producing Mosstowie malt.

fields.name: Linkwood
fields.description: Known for producing floral, sweet, and complex malts. Historically so valued that managers were forbidden from changing anything in production.

fields.name: Glen Elgin
fields.description: The last distillery built in the Victorian boom, producing honeyed and fruity malts. A key component in White Horse blend.

fields.name: Mannochmore
fields.description: Built next to Glenlossie, producing light and floral malts. Briefly released as black-bottled Loch Dhu in the 1990s.

fields.name: Aultmore
fields.description: Produces grassy, fresh, and elegant malts. Known as the distillery that never advertised but remained highly regarded by blenders.

fields.name: Inchgower
fields.description: A coastal Speyside distillery producing sweet and slightly salty malts. An important component in Bells blend.

fields.name: Glenallachie
fields.description: Relaunched with impressive sherry-cask releases under Billy Walker. Quickly gaining recognition for quality and value.

fields.name: Speyburn
fields.description: Built in time to produce whisky for Queen Victoria's Jubilee, creating light and grassy malts. A popular entry-level single malt.

fields.name: Tormore
fields.description: A striking architectural gem designed by Sir Albert Richardson, producing elegant and nutty malts. The first new distillery built in the 20th century.

fields.name: Tomatin
fields.description: Once Scotland's largest distillery with 23 stills, producing soft and malty whiskies. The first Scottish distillery owned by a Japanese company.

fields.name: Craigellachie
fields.description: Known for sulphury, meaty character from old-fashioned worm tub condensers. A favorite among malt enthusiasts for its bold style.

fields.name: Glen Keith
fields.description: Chivas Brothers' first new distillery, producing light and fruity spirit. Pioneered triple distillation in Speyside and experimented with peated malt.

fields.name: Glentauchers
fields.description: A workhorse distillery producing grassy, malty spirit mainly for blends. Rarely released as a single malt but valued by blenders.

fields.name: Caperdonich
fields.description: Glen Grant's sister distillery across the road, demolished in 2010. Known as the secret distillery with limited single malt releases.

fields.name: Convalmore
fields.description: Closed by DCL and now owned by William Grant as warehousing. Rare independent bottlings show elegant, floral character.

fields.name: Pittyvaich
fields.description: Built next to Dufftown distillery, producing light and grassy malts. Demolished after only 18 years of intermittent production.

fields.name: Imperial
fields.description: Named to celebrate Queen Victoria's Diamond Jubilee, with checkered operating history. Demolished despite attempts to save it.

fields.name: Braeval
fields.description: Originally called Braes of Glenlivet, one of Speyside's highest and most remote distilleries. Produces light, floral malts primarily for blends.

fields.name: Auchroisk
fields.description: Built as a showcase distillery with modern design, producing nutty and slightly smoky malts. Released as The Singleton in some markets.

fields.name: Allt-a-Bhainne
fields.description: Built for Chivas blends, rarely seen as a single malt. Produces clean, grassy spirit in an isolated location.

fields.name: Benromach
fields.description: Rescued and revived by independent bottler Gordon & MacPhail, producing traditional lightly peated malts. A boutique distillery with hands-on approach.

fields.name: Speyside Distillery
fields.description: A modern small-scale distillery in the Cairngorms, producing Spey and Beinn Dubh brands. Built over many years by founder George Christie.

fields.name: Roseisle
fields.description: One of Scotland's newest and largest distilleries with 14 stills, built for efficiency and sustainability. Produces fruity spirit for Johnnie Walker.

fields.name: Glenmorangie
fields.description: Famous for Scotland's tallest stills and pioneering wood finishing techniques. Produces elegant, floral Highland malts with complex layers.

fields.name: Dalmore
fields.description: Known for sherried, rich malts and the iconic 12-pointed stag emblem. Home to some of the world's most expensive whisky releases.

fields.name: Oban
fields.description: A small coastal distillery with the town built around it, producing rich and slightly smoky West Highland malts. Part of the Classic Malts range.

fields.name: Clynelish
fields.description: Successor to the original distillery, producing waxy, fruity malts with coastal influence. A key component in Johnnie Walker Gold Label.

fields.name: Teaninich
fields.description: An innovative distillery using the first mechanical malting in Scotland. Produces grassy, herbal malts mainly for blends.

fields.name: Balblair
fields.description: One of Scotland's oldest distilleries, producing elegant and fruity malts. Known for vintage-dated releases rather than age statements.

fields.name: Old Pulteney
fields.description: The most northerly mainland distillery, producing slightly briny, maritime malts. Once known as the Manzanilla of the North.

fields.name: Glen Ord
fields.description: One of the few distilleries with its own maltings still in operation, producing rich and spicy malts. Marketed as The Singleton in some regions.

fields.name: Royal Brackla
fields.description: The first distillery to receive a Royal Warrant in 1833, producing elegant and sherried malts. Known as The King's Own Whisky.

fields.name: Dalwhinnie
fields.description: Scotland's highest working distillery at 1,164 feet, producing gentle and honeyed malts. Part of the Classic Malts range representing the Highlands.

fields.name: Aberfeldy
fields.description: Built by the Dewar family, producing honeyed and fruity malts from Golden Pitilie stream water. The heart of Dewar's blends.

fields.name: Blair Athol
fields.description: An attractive Victorian distillery in the village of Pitlochry, producing rich and spicy malts. A key component in Bells blend.

fields.name: Edradour
fields.description: Scotland's smallest traditional distillery, still using manual production methods. Produces rich, creamy malts and heavily peated Ballechin.

fields.name: Deanston
fields.description: Converted from a cotton mill, powered by the River Teith and self-sufficient in electricity. Produces honeyed, waxy malts with a creamy texture.

fields.name: Tullibardine
fields.description: Built on the site of a medieval brewery, producing delicate and grassy Highland malts. Known for diverse wine cask finishes.

fields.name: Ben Nevis
fields.description: At the foot of Britain's highest mountain, producing robust, waxy malts. Owned by Japanese company Nikka since 1989.

fields.name: Macduff
fields.description: Often bottled as Glen Deveron, producing nutty and fruity coastal malts. Known for unusual horizontal lyne arms creating a unique character.

fields.name: Fettercairn
fields.description: One of Scotland's oldest licensed distilleries with unique cooling rings on the stills. Produces tropical fruit and spicy malts.

fields.name: Glencadam
fields.description: An elegant Eastern Highland distillery producing creamy and fruity malts. Known as the rather delicate Brechin malt.

fields.name: Royal Lochnagar
fields.description: Received its Royal Warrant after a visit from Queen Victoria in 1848. Produces light, floral malts with a hint of smoke.

fields.name: Brora
fields.description: A legendary distillery closed in 1983 and reopened in 2021, producing heavily peated Highland malts. One of whisky's most sought-after names.

fields.name: Glenturret
fields.description: Claims to be Scotland's oldest working distillery, producing rich and nutty malts. Home to the Famous Grouse Experience.

fields.name: Ardmore
fields.description: One of the few Highland distilleries producing peated malt, creating sweet and smoky whiskies. The heart of Teacher's Highland Cream.

fields.name: Knockdhu
fields.description: Bottled as anCnoc to avoid confusion with Knockando, producing elegant and aromatic malts. A pioneer in peat level experimentation.

fields.name: Lagavulin
fields.description: Produces intensely peated, rich, and complex Islay malts with exceptional depth. Part of the Classic Malts range and a whisky icon.

fields.name: Laphroaig
fields.description: Famous for medicinal, iodine-rich heavily peated malts. The only whisky to carry a Royal Warrant from Prince Charles.

fields.name: Ardbeg
fields.description: Produces the peatiest regular release malts with smoky, sweet complexity. Has a devoted global following and annual limited editions.

fields.name: Bowmore
fields.description: Islay's oldest distillery, maintaining traditional floor maltings and producing balanced smoky and fruity malts. Home to some of the oldest whisky stocks.

fields.name: Bruichladdich
fields.description: A progressive distillery producing unpeated, peated, and heavily peated expressions including Octomore. Known for innovation and terroir focus.

fields.name: Caol Ila
fields.description: Islay's largest distillery by output, producing elegant smoky malts with sweet notes. The main peated malt in Johnnie Walker.

fields.name: Bunnahabhain
fields.description: The gentle Islay, traditionally producing unpeated maritime malts with nutty sweetness. Recently added peated expressions to the range.

fields.name: Kilchoman
fields.description: Islay's first new distillery in 124 years, farm-based and producing its own barley. Creates complex, smoky malts with a modern approach.

fields.name: Ardnahoe
fields.description: Islay's newest distillery built by independent bottler Hunter Laing. Produces heavily peated spirit with first releases highly anticipated.

fields.name: Port Ellen
fields.description: Legendary distillery closed in 1983, now being restored and reopened by Diageo. Original stocks fetch astronomical prices at auction.

fields.name: Auchentoshan
fields.description: Scotland's only remaining triple-distilled single malt, producing delicate and light Lowland whisky. Known as Glasgow's Malt Whisky.

fields.name: Glenkinchie
fields.description: Edinburgh's closest distillery, producing grassy and floral Lowland malts. Part of the Classic Malts range representing the Lowlands.

fields.name: Bladnoch
fields.description: Scotland's most southerly distillery, producing floral and delicate Lowland whisky. Recently revitalized under new ownership.

fields.name: Ailsa Bay
fields.description: A large modern distillery built adjacent to Girvan grain distillery. Produces both peated and unpeated spirit mainly for blends.

fields.name: Daftmill
fields.description: A seasonal farm distillery producing whisky between harvests. Extremely limited releases highly sought after by collectors.

fields.name: Kingsbarns
fields.description: A boutique distillery in Fife producing elegant fruity malts. Built in a converted farm with visitor experience focus.

fields.name: Lindores Abbey
fields.description: Built on the site of the abbey where whisky distillation was first recorded in Scotland in 1494. A spiritual home of Scotch whisky.

fields.name: Annandale
fields.description: Historic distillery revived after 100 years of closure, producing Man O'Sword peated and Man O'Words unpeated malts.

fields.name: Glasgow Distillery
fields.description: The first working distillery in Glasgow for over a century, producing single malt and gin. Home to the 1770 brand.

fields.name: Rosebank
fields.description: A legendary triple-distilled Lowland malt closed in 1993 and recently reopened by Diageo. Known for floral elegance and complexity.

fields.name: Borders Distillery
fields.description: The first whisky distillery in the Scottish Borders in over 180 years. Producing traditional Lowland-style single malt.

fields.name: InchDairnie
fields.description: A high-tech distillery focusing on innovation with unique processes. Producing RyeLaw rye whisky and experimental single malts.

fields.name: Springbank
fields.description: One of Scotland's few remaining independent family-owned distilleries, producing lightly peated 2.5 times distilled malt. Everything done on-site from malting to bottling.

fields.name: Glen Scotia
fields.description: One of only three remaining Campbeltown distilleries, producing coastal, slightly peated malts. Experiencing a quality renaissance.

fields.name: Glengyle
fields.description: Reopened in 2004 by Springbank owners, producing Kilkerran single malt. Helps revive Campbeltown's whisky heritage.

fields.name: Highland Park
fields.description: The world's most northerly distillery in Orkney, producing balanced smoky and honeyed malts. Uses traditional floor maltings with local peat.

fields.name: Scapa
fields.description: Orkney's second distillery near Scapa Flow, producing lighter and more delicate island malts than its neighbor. Uses unique Lomond-style wash still.

fields.name: Talisker
fields.description: Skye's only distillery, producing powerful, peppery, and smoky maritime malts. Part of the Classic Malts range and beloved worldwide.

fields.name: Tobermory
fields.description: Isle of Mull's only distillery, producing unpeated Tobermory and peated Ledaig expressions. One of the oldest commercial distilleries in Scotland.

fields.name: Jura
fields.description: The Isle of Jura's only distillery, producing lightly peated to heavily peated expressions. Essential to the island's small community.

fields.name: Arran
fields.description: Lochranza distillery, the first legal distillery on Arran in 160 years. Produces fruity and complex island malts, now with peated expressions.

fields.name: Lagg
fields.description: Arran's second distillery in the south of the island, focusing exclusively on heavily peated whisky. Complementing Lochranza's unpeated style.

fields.name: Raasay
fields.description: The Isle of Raasay's first legal distillery, producing lightly peated and peated expressions. A showcase for innovation and island terroir.

fields.name: Torabhaig
fields.description: Skye's second distillery, producing heavily peated Hebridean single malt. Built in a restored 19th century farm steading.

fields.name: Abhainn Dearg
fields.description: Scotland's most westerly distillery on the Isle of Lewis, producing small batch lightly peated malts. The first legal distillery in the Outer Hebrides.
